article.name: EvoX Genesis
article.summary: EvoX Genesis is an open-source software-development agent system that supplies project context from repository-local Markdown files scoped to an agent's repository path. Git versions project changes and SQLite stores runtime/task data; product behavior and performance were not measured.

who_what.text: The README describes Genesis as developed by the EvoX Group at The Hong Kong Polytechnic University and as an open-source system for software development with AI agents.
Genesis is a full development system with a desktop app, headless server, dashboard, and local MCP endpoint, not a standalone memory database.

architecture.text: Project context is organized by repository path. ContextNode represents a normalized relative path and repository identity; the agent context builder asks it to assemble text for the assigned node.

The renderer builds stages from applicable repository-root-to-node CONTEXT.md files and the global VCT context stage when available. It provides text to the agent prompt instead of ranking individual memory records.

The README describes Git as recording software versions and SQLite as storing runtime/task data. The separate per-agent task archive schema stores task and agent IDs, parent/depth, context path, objective/result, base/final commits, branch/archive refs, repo identity, usage/settings, and timestamps.

behavior.text: Write and update: project context is authored in repository-local CONTEXT.md files as ordinary project changes. The README describes candidate work in isolated Git worktrees and human review of diffs before accepted results carry forward. The inspected sources did not identify a separate memory-record write or patch API.

Retrieval: the inspected core path assembles path-specific context from ancestor files and the global VCT stage when available. This is explicit and structural; the reviewed path does not show vector search, semantic ranking, or a memory answerability/abstention decision. A separate cross-history recall path was not established.

Delete: the inspected documentation and code describe file context and Git project changes, but do not establish a memory-specific delete API, per-memory tombstone, or deletion propagation protocol. Deletion leakage was not tested. The separate task-archive API supports deleting task archive rows, not deleting project memory.

Scope: the in-repository context chain follows root-to-node paths, excluding sibling paths from that assembled string. A global VCT context stage is also included; access-control guarantees for it were not established.

Provenance: Git versions project changes, and task archives record task/agent and commit/ref metadata. The inspected model does not attach citations, trust, or confidence to each CONTEXT.md statement; task provenance does not prove a memory claim.

metrics.evidence: The inspected path assembles context from path-scoped files; no scoring or abstention policy was established.
Context files can be edited as repository changes; no correction accuracy or stale-value workload was evaluated.
No memory-specific deletion protocol was established from the inspected sources, and no deletion probes were run.
Root-to-node context assembly excludes sibling paths in the rendered chain; global-context authorization and runtime isolation were not exercised.
Task and commit provenance exists, but per-claim evidence links were not established.
No runtime timing or write-to-recall workload was run.
A byte cap is configured for context stages; no token, cost, or storage workload was measured.

limits.text: This review inspected the public README and selected current upstream context-tree, context-builder, and task-archive sources, not a running Genesis instance or every retrieval tool. It cannot establish answer quality, freshness, product-level authorization, global-context permissions, deletion correctness, or actual performance.
The context builder falls back to a path-only string if context assembly errors. The review did not execute this path or determine the operational frequency of such errors.

benchmark.note: No Genesis runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Source observations and the benchmark fixture are not measured results.
